approach: Set the range formula at angle θ equal to half the maximum range and solve for θ.

steps.text: Write the range at angle θ and the maximum range, both at the same speed u.
steps.equation: R(θ) = u²sin2θ / g, R_max = u² / g (at θ = 45°)

steps.text: Set the range at θ equal to half the maximum range.
Cancel u²/g from both sides and solve for 2θ, then θ.
steps.equation: sin2θ = ½, so 2θ = 30° or 150°, θ = 15° or 75°; of these only 15° is among the options

common_mistakes.text: Taking 2θ = 30° but then forgetting to divide by 2 gives θ = 30°.
Writing 2θ = 120° instead of 30° or 150°, by confusing sin 120° (which is √3/2) with ½, gives θ = 60°.
